# M78 exact hosted recipe local rehearsal

This runner is preparation for a single native rehearsal of root's unchanged `exerciseM78` recipe. No hosted execution, provider authentication, database creation, migration, private credential/configuration read or Git operation is performed by this runner. Imports do not connect. Root supplies a **new** clone of the actual encrypted schema20 application restore after the reviewed additive21 upgrade; the clone must be named `m78_ops_recipe_*` on loopback55472 with existing `supabase_admin` and `neuvetra_runtime` roles.

## Admission

`bun tools/staging/m78-recipe-rehearsal.ts` reads bounded JSON from stdin. Its `inspect` mode reads receipts, all application rows, current proof and retained actor memberships, returning the actual row digest and 121-input source map. It creates no journal and sends zero application POSTs. `run` additionally requires the exact inspect digest, independently reviewed source map, backup/restore/upgrade receipt pins and a new exclusive workspace `.superpowers/m78-recipe-*.jsonl` or `.tmp/m78-recipe-*.jsonl` path.

Input keys are `mode`, `database`, fixed `companyId`, `actorIds:{manager1,manager2,member}`, `migrationSha256`, `recipeSha256`, `runnerSha256`, `reviewedSourcePins`, `provenancePins`, `baselineRowsSha256`, and `journalPath`. Hashes are lowercase SHA256. `provenancePins` contains at least three distinct workspace receipt paths and their reviewed exact byte hashes. Root/independent review must establish their actual backup/restore/upgrade semantics: the runner checks their unchanged bytes, not a generic receipt-status approval service. Inspect does not require provenance/source-map/digest/journal values; root may omit those unused fields.

The runner verifies actual socket host/port/database/user, fixed project/profile, every21 native receipt against the current manifest, current reviewed runner/recipe hashes, literal static/dynamic relative import closure, fixed workspace/package/config resolver metadata and all21SQL/lockfile, existing empty M78, corporatev8, accepted M77 populationv4 and all nine retained M77 reports. This refuses the earlier preserved failed-M77 template used by the prior positive backend fixture. Manager1 must be the retained corporate creator and eligible company manager; manager2 is distinct and outside all captured corporate/source/discovery contributors; member is an actual member. Runtime methods still enforce their cumulative contributor/tenant policy. No accounts, memberships or global privileges are granted. The supplied actors are mapped to synthetic in-process local tokens; provider Auth is unused.

The local adapter constructs the already implemented database class with the separately verified local runtime connection, following existing native fixtures. It does not call or loosen the hosted factory's TLS/project/credential guards. A database-scoped session advisory lease prevents another invocation of this rehearsal runner from owning the same clone. A new exclusive journal is synced before the first POST. Root must keep all other writers out of this dedicated clone.

## Exactly one recipe execution

Root's `exerciseM78` is called once. Per-family actual API handlers, native authorities and existing browser decoders process the recipe. Each POST has a durable intent before invocation and a durable raw response hash/status/length outcome before semantic verification. Decoded envelopes are retained in `post_verified`. Every returned version/review/report is compared with an exact authorized native GET; generated report HTML and snapshot downloads are also compared as member. The caller permits only38 distinct successful recipe writes on supported tenant routes, with configured manager roles, no parallel writes and no retry.

Final closure requires exactly38 attempted201 writes, processv1/inventoryv1-v2, five reports, separate accepted process/inventory reviews, reconciled bounded synthetic status, all ten source heads and three discovery heads bound to the reviewed corporate successor, and unchanged entity/facility/source identities. A member independently reads and decodes the final register and every family current register. Exactly38 new request and audit rows are required across these families.

## Retention and limitations

All121 Neuvetra tables are captured before execution. Every old row remains present with exact canonical content and multiplicity. All old request, audit, version, review, statement, report, reservation and unrelated rows are preserved. Only this company's `version_id`/`revision` fields on the named family head tables may change; every other old head field is checked. No legacy head may be added. New rows are allowed only in the recipe's eight named family namespaces, only for the fixed company; unrelated tables remain exactly equal. Global role attributes/memberships are compared before/after. Final rows, source pins and register evidence are retained. This is old byte/content preservation, not a fresh independent full historical accounting review or catalog recovery attestation. Audit sequence rollback is not claimed.

Any failed status, transport/driver error, decoder error, append failure, source mutation or retention mismatch halts. The journal is never reset or automatically retried; a partial commit may exist and requires an independently reviewed new bounded decision. Even if an outcome is missing, a later attempt cannot silently complete it: the occupied journal and nonempty M78/different baseline refuse admission. All opened connections and the journal close in `finally`; provider sessions created are zero. The128MB journal/50MB-event limits are explicit fixed demonstration bounds, not customer scale guarantees. No claim about hosted performance, complete Scope1 release, production factors or professional assurance follows from a rehearsal.

## Preparation evidence

Author19 pure guard assertions passed, including wrong targets/company/actors/pins/journal path, missing provenance, permitted head-only updates, protected old requests/rows, forbidden other-tenant append and complete source closure. Strict targeted TypeScript passed. These were local source-only checks with **zero database connections and zero POSTs**. Actual native38-write execution is pending root-supplied fresh actual restore/upgrade and independent runner admission. Earlier backend positive fixtures and failures remain historical; they do not substitute for this exact-recipe rehearsal.

### RECIPE-R01 resolver metadata repair, candidate2

Independent review demonstrated that candidate1's relative-import byte map did not pin package exports controlling bare `@neuvetra/database` resolution. Candidate1 and its preparation evidence remain preserved; its map was insufficient to claim the runtime closure reviewed. Candidate2 adds fixed metadata pins for root `package.json` workspace maps and `tsconfig.base.json`; database package/TypeScript configs; API package/TypeScript configs and `config/typescript/api.json`; browser package/config references and `config/typescript/web.json`/`vite.json`. No resolver configuration or recipe behavior changed. The runner compares the exact121-input map before any database connection and again at completion. Locked external packages remain bound through `bun.lock`; this fixed map does not claim arbitrary resolver discovery.

Candidate2 author32 guard assertions and strict targeted TypeScript pass, with zero database connections or POSTs. These include all13 resolver metadata pins. Independent review and the exact38-POST fresh-actual-clone native rehearsal remain pending. Actual hosted archive default-ACL transfer repair is a separate reviewed gate; the runner does not create a target or bypass that restore/upgrade provenance.

### RCP-F01 response shape repair, September22

The first actual recipe rehearsal stopped after three successful POSTs. The third write retained corporate version9; the adapter treated its numeric `version:9` as an envelope and requested `/versions/undefined`, receiving404. Read-only native diagnosis confirms the exact version ID route returns200 and passes the corporate decoder. The failed clone and10-event journal SHA `1e50cbb88fecbc58170429e009b800ff391f1c915b730b66c4917c7cd20ad943` remain untouched; this repair grants no retry or continuation.

The adapter now distinguishes a flat legacy version record from an M78 version envelope before constructing the exact readback route. Embedded reviews use the same extraction. Fleet and stationary-equipment reviews instead require a fully decoded register with the exact roster ID and exactly one matching retained review ID/version ID, since those families keep reviews separately. The hosted harness's compact identity extraction had the same numeric-version error and is repaired separately in its own small helper, requiring a valid record ID before writing `post_verified`.

Author verification:14 tests/134 assertions and strict targeted TypeScript pass. The native read-only diagnostic sent zero POSTs and preserved the failed journal hash. Independent acceptance and a complete new38-write rehearsal on a separately admitted fresh clone remain required; these source checks do not claim the fixed recipe completed.

# M78 RCP-F01 author repair

Task `M78-RESUME-RECIPE-FIX-01`; author `/root/resume_recipe`, software engineering under root/CTO. Requested registry route applies; actual inherited model/effort are unknown. Root retains Git, hosted execution and shared records. No hosted operation or application POST was performed by this assignment.

## Diagnosis

The frozen September22 journal contains three201 outcomes and stops before verifying the corporate successor. A read-only native handler check on `m78_ops_recipe_20260922` confirms current corporate version9 is valid: old `decoded.version ?? decoded` selects numeric9, creating a404 `/versions/undefined`; selecting the record ID returns200 and passes `decodeCorporateVersion`. The journal remains SHA `1e50cbb88fecbc58170429e009b800ff391f1c915b730b66c4917c7cd20ad943`.

The same numeric extraction also affected legacy embedded review comparison and compact hosted identities. Fleet/equipment reviews have a separate additional adapter mismatch: the version does not embed a review; the decoded register holds `reviews`. Their review contract uses `versionId`; `rosterVersionId` belongs to reports. No application defect was established.

## Repair and evidence

- `m78RecipeVersionRecord` accepts flat numeric version records or nested M78 records after the actual family decoder, and requires a valid ID and positive integer revision.
- `m78RecipeRetainedReview` extracts an exact embedded review or uniquely selects the matching ID/version from decoded fleet/equipment register reviews. The caller verifies the register's roster ID against the POST route.
- `m78VerifiedIdentity` preserves flat legacy, review and report identities, unwraps object version envelopes, and refuses missing/invalid IDs before a hosted verification event.
- Focused author tests:14 passed,134 assertions. Cases cover every stream-ID field, numeric and object versions, malformed identities, wrong/missing/duplicate reviews and report/review identity preservation.
- Strict targeted TypeScript passed for both changed runners and their tests.
- Actual native diagnosis:0 POSTs, correct GET200, erroneous old GET404, exact decoded version ID preserved.

All accepted prior snapshots, failed clone and journal are retained. Independent review and a fresh full38-write recipe remain pending. No native recipe completion, hosted deployment, released method or customer-ready Scope1 claim follows.
